--- title: "A scenario grid" --- A scenario grid holds several campaigns run against one shared setting, built so that the campaign is the only thing that differs between the arms. The five arms below all start from the same district, at under-5 prevalence 0.45, pyrethroid resistance 0.30, and pyrethroid-only nets at 0.70 coverage. - **Withdraw the nets.** No campaign at all. This is the counterfactual the other four are measured against, and it is the arm that results if a campaign is not restated. - **Replace like for like** with pyrethroid-only nets at the same 0.70 coverage. - **Switch to PBO**, again at 0.70. - **Switch to pyrrole**, again at 0.70. - **PBO plus IRS at 0.60 plus LSM at 0.30.** Every arm carries the same `EirTarget`, so the baseline EIR is inverted from the same prevalence under the same current net mix. All five start from an identical transmission intensity and an identical pre-campaign trajectory. Any difference between them is caused by the campaign and nothing else. ## Building the grid The shared fields go in a dictionary. They are splatted into each `Scenario`, an idiom R writes as `do.call(Scenario, c(district, list(name = "PBO", ...)))`, and writing those fields out five times over instead would invite a typo in one arm's `Q0` that silently breaks the comparison the grid exists to make. ::: {#04dacfe1 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from estimint import run_scenarios from estimint.scenarios import Scenario, EirTarget district = dict( res_use=0.30, Q0=0.85, phi=0.80, seasonal=0.0, irs=0.0, py_only=0.70, # the nets in place today routine=0.0, eir_target=EirTarget(0.45, "prevalence"), ) grid = [ Scenario(name="Withdraw", **district), Scenario(name="Pyrethroid-only", itn_future=0.70, net_type_future="pyrethroid_only", **district), Scenario(name="PBO", itn_future=0.70, net_type_future="pyrethroid_pbo", **district), Scenario(name="Pyrrole", itn_future=0.70, net_type_future="pyrethroid_pyrrole", **district), Scenario(name="PBO + IRS + LSM", itn_future=0.70, net_type_future="pyrethroid_pbo", irs_future=0.60, lsm=0.30, **district), ] len(grid) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 5 ``` ::: ::: ## One call `run_scenarios` takes the list, loads the models once, and puts the five scenarios through the emulator as a single batch. Five arms cost barely more than one. ::: {#47fbc5fd .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} res = run_scenarios(grid) res.shape ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (5, 23) ``` ::: ::: Five rows come back, one per arm. The columns are the same twenty-three that a single scenario returns. ## The shared baseline Check the baseline columns first. If the five arms did not start from the same place, none of the comparisons that follow would mean anything. ::: {#5d62c3f0 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} res[["name", "dn0_use", "itn_use", "eir_baseline", "prev_y9"]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
name dn0_use itn_use eir_baseline prev_y9
0 Withdraw 0.311 0.7 31.960129 0.456028
1 Pyrethroid-only 0.311 0.7 31.960129 0.456028
2 PBO 0.311 0.7 31.960129 0.456028
3 Pyrrole 0.311 0.7 31.960129 0.456028
4 PBO + IRS + LSM 0.311 0.7 31.960129 0.456028
``` ::: ::: All five arms share the same `dn0_use`, the same `itn_use`, an `eir_baseline` of about 32 infectious bites per person per year, and a `prev_y9` of about 0.456 against the 0.45 that went in. They are indistinguishable up to the campaign. They diverge only after it. ## The summary table The campaign columns and the two endline outcomes are what the grid was built for. ::: {#b60cad90 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} res[[ "name", "net_future", "dn0_future", "itn_future", "irs_future", "lsm", "prev_endline", "cases_endline", ]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
name net_future dn0_future itn_future irs_future lsm prev_endline cases_endline
0 Withdraw none 0.00000 0.0 0.0 0.0 0.498149 2.127164
1 Pyrethroid-only pyrethroid_only 0.31100 0.7 0.0 0.0 0.483688 2.433113
2 PBO pyrethroid_pbo 0.48495 0.7 0.0 0.0 0.470118 2.412444
3 Pyrrole pyrethroid_pyrrole 0.55015 0.7 0.0 0.0 0.464200 2.389937
4 PBO + IRS + LSM pyrethroid_pbo 0.48495 0.7 0.6 0.3 0.038096 0.165287
``` ::: ::: Read the `dn0_future` column first. At resistance 0.30 a pyrethroid-only net kills about 0.31 of the mosquitoes that touch it, a PBO net about 0.48, and a pyrrole net about 0.55. The ordering of the three net arms follows from that column and nothing else, since every other covariate is held fixed. The combination arm carries the PBO `dn0_future` (the nets are the same nets) and adds spraying at 0.60 and larviciding at 0.30 on top, so the endline prevalence it reaches comes out an order of magnitude below any net-only arm. Swapping one net for another moves prevalence by a few points. Adding a second and a third vector-control measure moves it considerably further. ## Withdrawal The first row was built by passing the district dictionary and nothing else, with no `itn_future` and no `net_type_future`. It reports the values the defaults supply. ::: {#ec6916ea .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} res.loc[res["name"] == "Withdraw", ["net_future", "dn0_future", "itn_future", "irs_future"]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}
net_future dn0_future itn_future irs_future
0 none 0.0 0.0 0.0
``` ::: ::: `net_future` is `"none"`, `dn0_future` is 0, `itn_future` is 0, and the district has been modelled as stopping net distribution altogether. Note that no warning is raised. The call succeeds, the frame comes back, and the trajectory is plausible. The only indication is the rebound, and it reads as wrong only to a reader who was expecting the nets to continue. ::: {#d1c06c96 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np withdraw = res.loc[res["name"] == "Withdraw"].iloc[0] like_for_like = res.loc[res["name"] == "Pyrethroid-only"].iloc[0] float(withdraw["prev_endline"]), float(like_for_like["prev_endline"]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ``` (0.49814853072166443, 0.4836880564689636) ``` ::: ::: The withdrawal arm ends about one and a half prevalence points above like-for-like replacement, a gap small enough to be mistaken for noise by a reader who was not looking for it. The difference in cumulative case burden between the two is considerably larger, as [Trajectories and cases](comparing.qmd) works out. Keep the arm in the grid deliberately. It is the counterfactual that makes cases averted a meaningful quantity. ## See also [Trajectories and cases](comparing.qmd) plots the five arms and integrates the burden each campaign averts, and [Exporting results](exporting.qmd) gets the grid out of Python. Please see [Nets and dn0](../04-estimint/nets-and-dn0.qmd) for the resistance curves behind `dn0_future`.
